newsitem.title: CHINA: HK expects 12 mln tourists, spending $US 12.27bln.
newsitem.headline: HK expects 12 mln tourists, spending $US 12.27bln.

text.p: Hong Kong, now a special region of China, said on Friday it expects over 12 million tourists this year, spending $US12.27 billion, to keep the metropolis as East Asia's top tourist destination.

Hong Kong's Secretary for Economic Services Stephen Ip predicted these record visitor arrivals and tourism receipts for the territory in 1997, declaring: "Travel and tourism is now Hong Kong's number one foreign exchange earner."
"In this year we expect the number of overseas tourists to surge to a new record of over 12 million and they will spend as much as HK$95 billion here," Ip told a news briefing.
A total of 11.7 million visitors arrived in Hong Kong last year and spent about HK$82.46 billion ($US 10.65 billion)), government statistics showed.
"Hong Kong is the most popular tourist destination in the region and in terms of tourism receipts Hong Kong ranks number eight worldwide," he said.
He said since two-third of visitors currently arrived in Hong Kong by air, the opening of a big new airport at Chek Lap Kok in April 1998 will further boost tourism in Hong Kong.
The US$9.0 billion airport is expected to handle 87 million passengers and nine million tonnes of cargo per year when the second of its two runways opens by the end of 1998.
